title: Structural Theorems for de Sitter-Unruh Modified Inertia: What the First-Moment Closure Forbids
description:
Seven machine-verified structural results about the first-moment closure of a modified-inertia action with a horizon-derived acceleration scale a0 = (1/2) c sqrt(G rho_Lambda). Five are prohibitions, two are predictions.

Theorem 1. The first-moment identity u_mu Box_u u^mu = -|a|^2 holds POINTWISE on every timelike worldline, following from u.u = -1 alone -- not only the circular and helical cases previously verified. Theorem 2. The closure's argument is therefore |a|^2 >= 0 while the kernel's branch cut requires z <= -1/4, so Im K == 0 IDENTICALLY, for the mean motion and every perturbation at every order. Corollary: the MOND amplitude and any dissipative channel are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE, and the sign postulate is demoted from a parameter awaiting data to a label on a branch the working theory never evaluates -- independently confirmed by an 8.5-sigma exclusion of the alternative closure's universal drift from PSR J0737-3039 timing. Theorem 3. The phenomenological law is second order while the Euler-Lagrange equation of any L(x, xdot, xddot) is fourth order, and the degeneracy escape is closed because the acceleration Hessian is non-singular: NO local higher-derivative action reproduces the law, so the nonlocal form is REQUIRED. Theorem 4. Comoving FRW makes the frame field an exact zero mode of the operator and K(0+) = 0, so the modified-inertia term VANISHES IDENTICALLY on the cosmological background; since K ~ sqrt(z) there, no perturbative modified Friedmann equation exists. Theorem 5. The external-field effect is forced to quadrature with a VECTOR cross term, so the customary linear ansatz with a multiplying phase function is unavailable; the prediction is a DIPOLE rotation-curve asymmetry, attractor-faster, of 4.2-22.3 per cent, and INDEPENDENT OF THE a0 FOOTING. This retracts an earlier claim that pure modified inertia predicts exactly zero directional asymmetry. Proposition 6. The linear-response inertia is h(x) = 2x/sqrt(1+4x^2), not mu_fw. Proposition 7. Dispersion-supported systems discriminate the residual closure freedom: the ultralocal member places them exactly on the rotation relation (verified to 1.6e-15), an orbit-averaged member offsets them by -0.037 dex, and existing Local Group dwarf spheroidals already reach ~1.2-1.9 sigma -- an archival test requiring no new facility.

Scope is stated explicitly: the paper concerns internal structure only. It does not derive the value of the coefficient kappa = 1/2, nor Z, both of which remain postulated. The interpolating kernel nu(y) = sqrt(1+1/y) is credited to Milgrom (1999, Phys. Lett. A 253, 273, Eq. 9); the framework's distinctive content is the coefficient and the modified-inertia completion. Every number is produced by a committed script that exits non-zero on any failed internal check.
notes:
VERSION 2 -- SELF-CORRECTION AFTER A REAL-DATA CONFRONTATION. v1's Proposition 7 attached an observational forecast to its two propositions: '~1.2-1.9 sigma on 40-60 Local Group dwarfs, 3 sigma at N~150, both routes archival'. THAT FORECAST WAS WRONG AND IS RETRACTED IN v2. Running the test on the real McConnachie (2012) catalogue (VizieR J/AJ/144/4/catalog, 46 of 102 usable rows) shows it is SYSTEMATICS-LIMITED, not sample-limited: per-object scatter is 0.38-0.48 dex rather than the assumed 0.15-0.20, and the dominant error -- the stellar mass-to-light ratio -- is COHERENT across the sample, so sqrt(N) does not reduce it. Varying Upsilon_V over 1-4 moves the mean residual by 0.322 dex, 8.7x the 0.037 dex signal; matching the signal would need Upsilon_V to 19% against a literature spread of 50-100%. Propositions 7.1 and 7.2 are UNCHANGED -- a theorem and a calculation -- and Theorems 1-5 and Proposition 6 are untouched. Only the forecast built on Prop 7 fails. New Sections 9.1-9.2 give the real-catalogue confrontation and the one surviving route: the Upsilon direction has a -0.067/dex slope against log(g_bar/a0) while the closure offset is flat, so the two are partially separable over the 5.28 dex of dynamic range available -- which requires the closure offset computed ACROSS g_bar, not done here.

Five of the seven results SUBTRACT from the framework: they remove a postulate, a channel, a class of actions, and a cosmological sector from its reach. Two prior claims in the author's own corpus are retracted here: that pure modified inertia predicts exactly zero directional asymmetry (Theorem 5), and the treatment of the sign as a parameter awaiting data (Corollary 2.2). The moment-identity-versus-Euler-Lagrange gap of Section 5 is recorded as unresolved, the MOND saddle region of Section 7 as outside the validity of the point-particle treatment, and the Section 9 orbit calculation as planar and idealised.
